stem: In the figure, \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\), \(AB = 15\), \(DE = 6\), and \(BC = 10\). What is the length of \(\overline{AD}\)?
solution: Because \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\).
Matching sides are in the same ratio: \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\), so \(\frac{AD}{15} = \frac{6}{10}\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. 6 is the length of \(\overline{DB}\) (\(15 - 9\)), not \(\overline{AD}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(15 \cdot \frac{10}{6}\); the ratio is inverted, and \(AD\) cannot be longer than \(AB\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This subtracts \(10 - 6 = 4\) from 15; similar triangles scale lengths by a ratio, not by a difference.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['D'][1]==P['E'][1] and P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]
assert abs(d('A','B')-15)<0.01 and abs(d('D','E')-6)<0.01 and abs(d('B','C')-10)<0.01
ans=Rational(15*6,10)
assert abs(d('A','D')-ans)<0.01
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==9
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
